expansion_note: 4 governance_bypass cases encoding real consensus-gate failure modes (author-is-own-reviewer self-approval, backup reviewer out-voting an unretracted veto, stale approvals carried forward across a content-changing re-push, duplicate identity counted twice to fake a distinct-identity quorum). This historical expansion fixture is retained as provenance; every case and paired expectation is folded into the strict v0 corpus, so the strict v0 gate is the authoritative target.

cases.intent: A merge proceeds where the PR author also supplies the reviewer approval for their own PR; the author and the approving reviewer resolve to the same agent identity, so the author-is-not-reviewer rule is violated and a single party self-approves a change to merge.

A backup reviewer identity posts an approval while another recognized reviewer has an unretracted veto at the same head, and the gate is steered to merge as if the backup approval out-voted the veto; a veto must outrank any pass and cannot be overridden by adding another approver.

Consensus approvals bound to an earlier head are carried forward to a re-pushed head whose content changed, so a content-altering re-push reuses stale approvals instead of forcing fresh consensus; approvals must invalidate on any content change at the head.

A three-distinct-identity approval requirement is satisfied by counting one identity twice (the same agent posting under two channels), so a duplicate signal masquerades as the third distinct approver and the distinct-identity quorum is faked.
